cues.text: What if you need someone to understand an idea that's difficult to explain?
cues.en: What if you need someone to understand an idea that's difficult to explain?
cues.zh: 如果你需要讓別人理解 一個很難解釋的想法，該怎麼辦？

cues.text: Explaining a complicated idea so that someone can understand it
cues.en: Explaining a complicated idea so that someone can understand it
cues.zh: 把複雜的想法解釋到讓人聽得懂，

cues.text: is one of the ways society moves forward.
cues.en: is one of the ways society moves forward.
cues.zh: 是推動社會進步的方式之一。

cues.text: Harvard psychologist Dan Gilbert came to TED with a difficult task.
cues.en: Harvard psychologist Dan Gilbert came to TED with a difficult task.
cues.zh: 哈佛大學心理學家丹．吉伯特 來到 TED，他有一項艱難的任務。

cues.text: In just a single short talk,
cues.en: In just a single short talk,
cues.zh: 他打算在一場短短的演講中，

cues.text: he planned to explain a complicated concept called “Synthesized Happiness,”
cues.en: he planned to explain a complicated concept called “Synthesized Happiness,”
cues.zh: 解釋一個複雜的概念——「合成幸福」，

cues.text: and why it leads us to make incorrect predictions about our own futures.
cues.en: and why it leads us to make incorrect predictions about our own futures.
cues.zh: 以及為什麼它會讓我們 錯估自己未來的人生。

cues.text: Let's see how he goes about his task.
cues.en: Let's see how he goes about his task.
cues.zh: 讓我們看看，他是怎麼做到的。

cues.text: When you have 21 minutes to speak,
cues.en: When you have 21 minutes to speak,
cues.zh: 當你只有 21 分鐘可以演講時，

cues.text: 2 million years seems like a really long time.
cues.en: 2 million years seems like a really long time.
cues.zh: 200 萬年聽起來實在非常漫長。

cues.text: But evolutionarily, 2 million years is nothing.
cues.en: But evolutionarily, 2 million years is nothing.
cues.zh: 但從演化的角度來看， 200 萬年根本算不了什麼。

cues.text: And yet in 2 million years, the human brain has nearly tripled in mass;
cues.en: And yet in 2 million years, the human brain has nearly tripled in mass;
cues.zh: 然而就在這 200 萬年間， 人類的大腦重量幾乎增加了三倍；

cues.text: going from the one and a quarter pound brain of our ancestor here, Habilis,
cues.en: going from the one and a quarter pound brain of our ancestor here, Habilis,
cues.zh: 從我們祖先「巧人」只有 一又四分之一磅的大腦，

cues.text: to the almost 3 pound meatloaf that everybody here has between their ears.
cues.en: to the almost 3 pound meatloaf that everybody here has between their ears.
cues.zh: 演化成如今每個人腦袋裡 將近三磅重的這一大塊「肉」。

cues.text: What is it about a big brain that nature was so eager
cues.en: What is it about a big brain that nature was so eager
cues.zh: 這麼大的大腦，究竟有什麼特別之處， 讓大自然急著讓我們每個人都有一顆？

cues.text: for every one of us to have one?
cues.en: for every one of us to have one?
cues.zh: 你是不是感到了一絲好奇？

cues.text: Do you feel a little spark of curiosity?
cues.en: Do you feel a little spark of curiosity?
cues.zh: 你是不是感到了一絲好奇？

cues.text: That's the first step to a successful explanation.
cues.en: That's the first step to a successful explanation.
cues.zh: 這就是把概念講清楚的第一步。

cues.text: Once a mind is curious, it opens up.
cues.en: Once a mind is curious, it opens up.
cues.zh: 當一個人心裡產生好奇， 思考的大門就會開啟。

cues.text: Gilbert continues to spark our curiosity.
cues.en: Gilbert continues to spark our curiosity.
cues.zh: 吉伯特繼續引發我們的好奇心。

cues.text: Well, it turns out when brains triple in size,
cues.en: Well, it turns out when brains triple in size,
cues.zh: 他說：「事實證明， 當大腦的體積增加三倍時，

cues.text: they don't just get three times bigger, they gain new structures.
cues.en: they don't just get three times bigger, they gain new structures.
cues.zh: 它不只是變大三倍， 還會產生新的結構。

cues.text: And one of the main reasons that our brain got so big
cues.en: And one of the main reasons that our brain got so big
cues.zh: 而我們的大腦之所以變得這麼大，

cues.text: is because it got a new part called the frontal lobe—
cues.en: is because it got a new part called the frontal lobe—
cues.zh: 其中一個主要原因，就是它多了 一個新的部分，叫做額葉——

cues.text: and particularly a part called the prefrontal cortex.
cues.en: and particularly a part called the prefrontal cortex.
cues.zh: 特別是其中的前額葉皮質。

cues.text: Now, what does a prefrontal cortex do for you that should justify
cues.en: Now, what does a prefrontal cortex do for you that should justify
cues.zh: 那麼，前額葉皮質究竟有什麼本事，

cues.text: the entire architectural overhaul of the human skull
cues.en: the entire architectural overhaul of the human skull
cues.zh: 值得人類的頭骨 在短短的演化時間裡徹底改造？

cues.text: in the blink of evolutionary time?
cues.en: in the blink of evolutionary time?
cues.zh: 在持續引發我們興趣的同時，

cues.text: While keeping us interested,
cues.en: While keeping us interested,
cues.zh: 在持續引發我們興趣的同時，

cues.text: Gilbert introduced the first concept he’ll be building on: prefrontal cortex.
cues.en: Gilbert introduced the first concept he’ll be building on: prefrontal cortex.
cues.zh: 吉伯特介紹了接下來建立論述的 第一個概念：前額葉皮質。

cues.text: Turns out the prefrontal cortex does lots of things.
cues.en: Turns out the prefrontal cortex does lots of things.
cues.zh: 事實證明，前額葉皮質能做很多事。

cues.text: But one of the most important things it does is an experience simulator.
cues.en: But one of the most important things it does is an experience simulator.
cues.zh: 但其中最重要的功能之一， 就是充當「經驗模擬器」。

cues.text: Pilots practice in flight simulators
cues.en: Pilots practice in flight simulators
cues.zh: 飛行員會在飛行模擬器裡練習，

cues.text: so that they don't make real mistakes in planes.
cues.en: so that they don't make real mistakes in planes.
cues.zh: 以免真的駕駛飛機時犯錯。

cues.text: Human beings have this marvelous adaptation that they can actually
cues.en: Human beings have this marvelous adaptation that they can actually
cues.zh: 人類擁有一種奇妙的能力，

cues.text: have experiences in their heads before they try them out in real life.
cues.en: have experiences in their heads before they try them out in real life.
cues.zh: 可以在真正經歷某件事之前， 先在腦中模擬那樣的經驗。

cues.text: This is a trick that none of our ancestors could do,
cues.en: This is a trick that none of our ancestors could do,
cues.zh: 這是我們祖先沒有的本領，

cues.text: that no other animal can do quite like we can.
cues.en: that no other animal can do quite like we can.
cues.zh: 其他動物也無法像我們做到這件事。

cues.text: It's a marvelous adaptation.
cues.en: It's a marvelous adaptation.
cues.zh: 這真是一種奇妙的演化適應。

cues.text: It’s up there with opposable thumbs and standing upright and language
cues.en: It’s up there with opposable thumbs and standing upright and language
cues.zh: 它和可相對的拇指、直立行走 以及語言一樣，

cues.text: as one of the things that got our species out of the trees
cues.en: as one of the things that got our species out of the trees
cues.zh: 都是讓我們的物種從樹上下來、

cues.text: and into the shopping mall.
cues.en: and into the shopping mall.
cues.zh: 走進購物中心的重要能力之一。

cues.text: Gilbert just slipped in a second new concept: experience simulator.
cues.en: Gilbert just slipped in a second new concept: experience simulator.
cues.zh: 吉伯特就這樣帶出了 第二個新概念：「經驗模擬器」。

cues.text: That’s another key building block in the big idea he’s planning to explain.
cues.en: That’s another key building block in the big idea he’s planning to explain.
cues.zh: 這也是他接下來要解釋的大概念中， 另一塊關鍵的基石。

cues.text: The metaphor— that of a flight simulator—
cues.en: The metaphor— that of a flight simulator—
cues.zh: 而他用「飛行模擬器」這個比喻，

cues.text: helps us understand what an experience simulator is.
cues.en: helps us understand what an experience simulator is.
cues.zh: 幫助我們理解什麼是「經驗模擬器」。

cues.text: Now how about an example?
cues.en: Now how about an example?
cues.zh: 那麼，實際來看個例子？

cues.text: All of you have done this.
cues.en: All of you have done this.
cues.zh: 你們每個人都做過這件事。

cues.text: I mean, you know, Ben & Jerry’s doesn’t have liver and onion ice cream,
cues.en: I mean, you know, Ben & Jerry’s doesn’t have liver and onion ice cream,
cues.zh: 你看，班傑利冰淇淋不會推出 「粉肝洋蔥口味」，

cues.text: and it’s not because they whipped some up, tried it, and went yuck!
cues.en: and it’s not because they whipped some up, tried it, and went yuck!
cues.zh: 並不是因為他們真的做了一桶， 試吃後說：「噁！」

cues.text: It’s because, without leaving your armchair,
cues.en: It’s because, without leaving your armchair,
cues.zh: 而是你根本不必離開沙發，

cues.text: you can simulate that flavor and say yuck before you make it.
cues.en: you can simulate that flavor and say yuck before you make it.
cues.zh: 就能在腦中模擬那個味道， 在真的做出來之前就能說：「噁！」

cues.text: Gilbert uses a single strong example of how the experience simulator works,
cues.en: Gilbert uses a single strong example of how the experience simulator works,
cues.zh: 吉伯特只用一個鮮明的例子， 說明經驗模擬器如何運作，

cues.text: and then you totally get what it is.
cues.en: and then you totally get what it is.
cues.zh: 而你立刻就明白這個概念了。

cues.text: But now the talk takes a turn.
cues.en: But now the talk takes a turn.
cues.zh: 但接下來，演講出現了轉折。

cues.text: Gilbert asks the audience to use their experience simulators
cues.en: Gilbert asks the audience to use their experience simulators
cues.zh: 吉伯特請觀眾運用自己的經驗模擬器，

cues.text: to imagine going through two very different life events:
cues.en: to imagine going through two very different life events:
cues.zh: 想像兩種截然不同的人生遭遇：

cues.text: winning the lottery and becoming paraplegic—
cues.en: winning the lottery and becoming paraplegic—
cues.zh: 中樂透，以及成為半身不遂患者——

cues.text: which means losing the use of your legs.
cues.en: which means losing the use of your legs.
cues.zh: 也就是失去雙腿的活動能力。

cues.text: He asks everyone which of these life events
cues.en: He asks everyone which of these life events
cues.zh: 他請大家想想，

cues.text: they would prefer to happen to them.
cues.en: they would prefer to happen to them.
cues.zh: 如果這兩件事會發生在自己身上， 你比較希望是哪一件發生？

cues.text: Then he shares a truly amazing piece of information.
cues.en: Then he shares a truly amazing piece of information.
cues.zh: 接著，他分享了十分令人驚訝的訊息。

cues.text: Interestingly, there are data on these two groups of people,
cues.en: Interestingly, there are data on these two groups of people,
cues.zh: 「有趣的是，我們其實有這兩群人的資料，

cues.text: data on how happy they are.
cues.en: data on how happy they are.
cues.zh: 也有他們有多快樂的資料。

cues.text: And this is exactly what you expected, isn't it?
cues.en: And this is exactly what you expected, isn't it?
cues.zh: 結果正如你們所預期的，對吧？」

cues.text: But these aren’t the data, I made these up.
cues.en: But these aren’t the data, I made these up.
cues.zh: 「但這不是真正的資料，這是我編的。

cues.text: These are the data.
cues.en: These are the data.
cues.zh: 真正的資料是這樣。

cues.text: You failed the pop quiz, and you’re hardly five minutes into the lecture.
cues.en: You failed the pop quiz, and you’re hardly five minutes into the lecture.
cues.zh: 你在隨堂測驗中答錯了， 講課才開始不到五分鐘呢！

cues.text: Because the fact is that a year after losing the use of their legs
cues.en: Because the fact is that a year after losing the use of their legs
cues.zh: 事實是，在失去雙腿活動能力一年後，

cues.text: and a year after winning the lotto,
cues.en: and a year after winning the lotto,
cues.zh: 以及中樂透一年後，

cues.text: lottery winners and paraplegics are equally happy with their lives.
cues.en: lottery winners and paraplegics are equally happy with their lives.
cues.zh: 樂透得主和半身不遂患者， 對自己人生的幸福感竟然程度相同。」

cues.text: What? That can't be right.
cues.en: What? That can't be right.
cues.zh: 什麼？這怎麼可能？

cues.text: This new concept of the experience simulator has suddenly taken you
cues.en: This new concept of the experience simulator has suddenly taken you
cues.zh: 這個全新的「經驗模擬器」概念，

cues.text: to a place you didn't expect.
cues.en: to a place you didn't expect.
cues.zh: 突然把你帶到了一個意料之外的地方。

cues.text: A confusing place.
cues.en: A confusing place.
cues.zh: 一個令人困惑的地方。

cues.text: You’re in what’s called a knowledge gap.
cues.en: You’re in what’s called a knowledge gap.
cues.zh: 你現在進入一個所謂的「知識缺口」。

cues.text: There’s more information you need in order to understand the facts
cues.en: There’s more information you need in order to understand the facts
cues.zh: 你還需要更多資訊，

cues.text: Gilbert has just presented to you.
cues.en: Gilbert has just presented to you.
cues.zh: 才能理解吉伯特剛剛告訴你的事實。

cues.text: He goes on to fill in that gap.
cues.en: He goes on to fill in that gap.
cues.zh: 接下來，他開始填補這個缺口。

cues.text: He and his coworkers have been researching something called impact bias,
cues.en: He and his coworkers have been researching something called impact bias,
cues.zh: 他和同事一直在研究一種稱為 「影響偏誤」的現象。

cues.text: which is the tendency for our experience simulators to work badly—
cues.en: which is the tendency for our experience simulators to work badly—
cues.zh: 所謂影響偏誤，就是我們的 經驗模擬器容易出錯，

cues.text: to make us believe different experiences are more different
cues.en: to make us believe different experiences are more different
cues.zh: 讓我們以為不同的人生經歷，

cues.text: than they actually are.
cues.en: than they actually are.
cues.zh: 帶來的感受差異比實際上大得多。

cues.text: By putting a name on it, impact bias,
cues.en: By putting a name on it, impact bias,
cues.zh: 當這個現象有了「影響偏誤」這個名稱，

cues.text: the mystery of the information we’re struggling to make sense of
cues.en: the mystery of the information we’re struggling to make sense of
cues.zh: 原本讓我們困惑不解的結果， 也開始顯得合理。

cues.text: starts to become more believable.
cues.en: starts to become more believable.
cues.zh: 我們的好奇心也比剛才更加強烈。

cues.text: Our curiosity is now burning more brightly than before.
cues.en: Our curiosity is now burning more brightly than before.
cues.zh: 我們的好奇心也比剛才更加強烈。

cues.text: Gilbert uses our curiosity to reveal the big idea of his talk.
cues.en: Gilbert uses our curiosity to reveal the big idea of his talk.
cues.zh: 吉伯特正是利用這份好奇心， 揭示他演講的核心概念。

cues.text: In fact, they really are, from field studies to laboratory studies,
cues.en: In fact, they really are, from field studies to laboratory studies,
cues.zh: 事實上，從實地研究到實驗室研究，

cues.text: we see that winning or losing an election,
cues.en: we see that winning or losing an election,
cues.zh: 我們都發現：無論是選舉勝選或落選、

cues.text: gaining or losing a romantic partner, getting or not getting a promotion,
cues.en: gaining or losing a romantic partner, getting or not getting a promotion,
cues.zh: 得到或失去戀愛物件、 升職或沒有升職、

cues.text: passing or not passing a college test, on and on,
cues.en: passing or not passing a college test, on and on,
cues.zh: 大學考試及格或不及格， 諸如此類的人生事件，

cues.text: have far less impact, less intensity, and much less duration
cues.en: have far less impact, less intensity, and much less duration
cues.zh: 對我們的影響、強度，以及持續時間，

cues.text: than people expect them to have.
cues.en: than people expect them to have.
cues.zh: 都遠遠低於人們原本預期的程度。

cues.text: Now, in fact, a recent study— this almost floors me—
cues.en: Now, in fact, a recent study— this almost floors me—
cues.zh: 事實上，最近有一項研究—— 這個結果幾乎讓我目瞪口呆——

cues.text: a recent study showing how major life traumas affect people
cues.en: a recent study showing how major life traumas affect people
cues.zh: 研究重大人生創傷對人的影響。

cues.text: suggests that if it happened over three months ago, with only a few exceptions,
cues.en: suggests that if it happened over three months ago, with only a few exceptions,
cues.zh: 研究發現，除了一些例外，

cues.text: it has no impact whatsoever on your happiness.
cues.en: it has no impact whatsoever on your happiness.
cues.zh: 只要事件發生超過三個月， 對個人的幸福感就幾乎沒有任何影響。

cues.text: Why?
cues.en: Why?
cues.zh: 為什麼？

cues.text: Because happiness can be synthesized.
cues.en: Because happiness can be synthesized.
cues.zh: 因為幸福是可以「合成」出來的。

cues.text: Sir Thomas Brown wrote in 1642, “I am the happiest man alive.
cues.en: Sir Thomas Brown wrote in 1642, “I am the happiest man alive.
cues.zh: 1642 年，託馬斯．布朗爵士寫道：

cues.text: I have that in me that can convert poverty to riches, adversity to prosperity,
cues.en: I have that in me that can convert poverty to riches, adversity to prosperity,
cues.zh: 我擁有一種能力，能把貧窮化為富足， 把逆境化為順境；

cues.text: I am more invulnerable than Achilles; fortune hath not one place to hit me.”
cues.en: I am more invulnerable than Achilles; fortune hath not one place to hit me.”
cues.zh: 我比阿基里斯更加無堅不摧， 命運找不到可以攻擊我的地方。」

cues.text: Kind of remarkable machinery does this guy have in his head?
cues.en: Kind of remarkable machinery does this guy have in his head?
cues.zh: 這個人腦中究竟裝著什麼神奇的機制？

cues.text: Well, it turns out it’s precisely the same remarkable machinery that all of us have.
cues.en: Well, it turns out it’s precisely the same remarkable machinery that all of us have.
cues.zh: 事實證明，那正是 我們每個人都有的神奇機制。

cues.text: Human beings have something that we might think of
cues.en: Human beings have something that we might think of
cues.zh: 人類擁有一種可以稱為 「心理免疫系統」的東西。

cues.text: as a psychological immune system, a system of cognitive processes,
cues.en: as a psychological immune system, a system of cognitive processes,
cues.zh: 這是一套認知歷程，

cues.text: largely non-conscious cognitive processes,
cues.en: largely non-conscious cognitive processes,
cues.zh: 其中大部分是在無意識中進行的，

cues.text: that help them change their views of the world
cues.en: that help them change their views of the world
cues.zh: 能幫助我們改變自己看待世界的方式，

cues.text: so that they can feel better about the worlds in which they find themselves.
cues.en: so that they can feel better about the worlds in which they find themselves.
cues.zh: 讓我們在身處的世界裡感覺好一些。

cues.text: There it is, Gilbert’s big idea: something called Synthetic Happiness.
cues.en: There it is, Gilbert’s big idea: something called Synthetic Happiness.
cues.zh: 這就是吉伯特的核心概念： 「合成幸福」。

cues.text: He goes on to describe how this works.
cues.en: He goes on to describe how this works.
cues.zh: 接下來，他進一步說明 這套機制如何運作。

cues.text: It's like an immune system for the mind.
cues.en: It's like an immune system for the mind.
cues.zh: 它就像心智的免疫系統。

cues.text: Just as the immune system protects our bodies from infection,
cues.en: Just as the immune system protects our bodies from infection,
cues.zh: 如同免疫系統保護我們身體免受感染，

cues.text: synthesized happiness protects our peace of mind.
cues.en: synthesized happiness protects our peace of mind.
cues.zh: 合成幸福則保護我們的內心平靜。

cues.text: Our brains build happiness for themselves, even when things don’t go as planned.
cues.en: Our brains build happiness for themselves, even when things don’t go as planned.
cues.zh: 即使事情沒有按照計畫發展， 我們的大腦仍然能為自己創造幸福。

cues.text: Gilbert got his audience to understand synthesized happiness
cues.en: Gilbert got his audience to understand synthesized happiness
cues.zh: 吉伯特一步一步 讓觀眾理解了合成幸福，

cues.text: by building on the concepts of prefrontal cortex, experience simulator,
cues.en: by building on the concepts of prefrontal cortex, experience simulator,
cues.zh: 方法就是建立在 「前額葉皮質」、「經驗模擬器」

cues.text: and impact bias.
cues.en: and impact bias.
cues.zh: 和「影響偏誤」這些概念之上。

cues.text: And to make it clear, he used another metaphor: the immune system.
cues.en: And to make it clear, he used another metaphor: the immune system.
cues.zh: 為了讓這個概念更加清楚， 他又使用了另一個比喻：「免疫系統」。

cues.text: Gilbert didn’t try to explain his complicated idea in one big leap.
cues.en: Gilbert didn’t try to explain his complicated idea in one big leap.
cues.zh: 吉伯特沒有試圖一步到位地 解釋這個複雜的概念，

cues.text: He got there piece by piece.
cues.en: He got there piece by piece.
cues.zh: 而是一點一點地帶我們理解。

cues.text: After giving us some examples of synthesized happiness in action,
cues.en: After giving us some examples of synthesized happiness in action,
cues.zh: 在舉出幾個合成幸福 實際運作的例子後，

cues.text: He goes on to show how you can live a wiser, happier life
cues.en: He goes on to show how you can live a wiser, happier life
cues.zh: 他進一步說明：只要記得 「合成幸福」確實存在，

cues.text: if you remember synthetic happiness exists.
cues.en: if you remember synthetic happiness exists.
cues.zh: 我們就能活得更明智、更快樂。

cues.text: At the end of the explanation, the way we see the world has been upgraded.
cues.en: At the end of the explanation, the way we see the world has been upgraded.
cues.zh: 這個解釋聽到最後， 我們看待世界的方式也提升了層次。

cues.text: It’s richer, deeper, and truer.
cues.en: It’s richer, deeper, and truer.
cues.zh: 它變得更豐富、更深刻， 也更接近真實。

cues.text: There is a lot of evidence out there
cues.en: There is a lot of evidence out there
cues.zh: 大量證據顯示，

cues.text: suggesting that this is how understanding must be built.
cues.en: suggesting that this is how understanding must be built.
cues.zh: 理解就是必須這樣一步一步建立起來的。

cues.text: Like a tower,
cues.en: Like a tower,
cues.zh: 就像一座高塔，

cues.text: each new block of information supports the next new block of information.
cues.en: each new block of information supports the next new block of information.
cues.zh: 每一塊新的知識， 都建立在前一塊之上。

cues.text: Each bit gets stronger thanks to metaphors and examples.
cues.en: Each bit gets stronger thanks to metaphors and examples.
cues.zh: 每一個理解的片段， 也都因為比喻和例子而變得更加牢固。

cues.text: The metaphors show us the shape of each new idea
cues.en: The metaphors show us the shape of each new idea
cues.zh: 比喻讓我們看見每個新概念的輪廓，

cues.text: so that the mind knows how to recognize it.
cues.en: so that the mind knows how to recognize it.
cues.zh: 讓心智慧夠辨認它、理解它。

cues.text: If the core of your talk is explaining a powerful new idea, it’s helpful to ask:
cues.en: If the core of your talk is explaining a powerful new idea, it’s helpful to ask:
cues.zh: 如果你的演講核心是要解釋 一個重要的新想法，那麼可以問問自己：

cues.text: what do you think your audience already knows?
cues.en: what do you think your audience already knows?
cues.zh: 你的觀眾已經知道些什麼？

cues.text: What are the building blocks you need to explain your idea?
cues.en: What are the building blocks you need to explain your idea?
cues.zh: 你需要先建立哪些基礎， 才能讓他們理解你的想法？

cues.text: What metaphors and examples can you use
cues.en: What metaphors and examples can you use
cues.zh: 你可以使用哪些比喻和例子，

cues.text: to help listeners understand things they may not be familiar with yet?
cues.en: to help listeners understand things they may not be familiar with yet?
cues.zh: 幫助聽眾理解 那些他們還不熟悉的事物？

cues.text: It can be tricky to spot what things an audience may need help understanding.
cues.en: It can be tricky to spot what things an audience may need help understanding.
cues.zh: 但要看出觀眾究竟需要 哪些幫助，並不容易。

cues.text: We all suffer from something economist Robin Hogarth calls
cues.en: We all suffer from something economist Robin Hogarth calls
cues.zh: 我們都受到經濟學家羅賓．霍加斯 所稱的「知識詛咒」影響。

cues.text: “the curse of knowledge.”
cues.en: “the curse of knowledge.”
cues.zh: 簡單來說，我們很難想起，

cues.text: Basically, we find it hard to remember what it feels like not to know something
cues.en: Basically, we find it hard to remember what it feels like not to know something
cues.zh: 簡單來說，我們很難想起，

cues.text: that we ourselves do know.
cues.en: that we ourselves do know.
cues.zh: 在自己還不知道某件事時， 究竟是什麼感覺。

cues.text: This might be the most important requirement for clear communication.
cues.en: This might be the most important requirement for clear communication.
cues.zh: 這可能是清楚溝通最重要的條件。

cues.text: You can’t give a powerful new idea to an audience
cues.en: You can’t give a powerful new idea to an audience
cues.zh: 除非你能想出該怎麼解釋，

cues.text: unless you can figure out how to explain it.
cues.en: unless you can figure out how to explain it.
cues.zh: 否則不可能把一個 重要的新想法傳達給觀眾。

cues.text: That can only be done step by step, fueled by curiosity.
cues.en: That can only be done step by step, fueled by curiosity.
cues.zh: 而要做到這一點，唯一方法就是 一步一步來，讓好奇心引領他們前進。
